batch.askedNote: {items} is Ask each time (add request: true to execute: true and the app asks for permission when the batch runs)
batch.broken.targetGone: What {via} of {at} points to is missing
batch.failed.added: steps[{step}] ({tool}) does not go through: {error}. Nothing was staged
batch.failed.earlier: {step}, staged earlier, does not go through in the project as it is now: {error}. Nothing was staged
batch.failed.later: . "{path}" is made by the later steps[{later}] ({tool}). Steps run in order, so put the step that makes it first (a flow's nodes made in one card_create, with no target and value keyed by path, may point at each other in any order)
batch.failed.opened: steps[{index}] ({tool}) failed: {error}. Nothing was written (everything was rolled back)
batch.failed.removal: Removing it would make {step} fail: {error}. It was not removed
batch.failed.retry: {step} does not go through: {error}. Nothing was changed. Take it out with remove in value, or stage the steps again to fit the project as it is now
batch.failed.run: {step} failed: {error}. Nothing was written (everything was rolled back). The batch is kept as it was
batch.open.missing: There is no batch "{token}" — it was run or discarded, or cleared away after 7 days untouched. Open the batch again with batch
batch.open.needsProject: project is needed to try steps or open a batch (to continue a staged batch, give its id as target)
batch.run.empty: Nothing has been staged in this batch yet
batch.step.label: steps[{offset}] ({name})
batch.step.noBranch: {label}: do not write branch in a step's arguments (steps write to the batch's {tree}; the tree is named with branch of batch when the batch is opened)
batch.step.notBatchable: This tool cannot be staged in a batch
batch.step.otherProject: {label}: project differs from this batch's project
batch.steps.elementShape: Each element of steps is {tool, arguments}
batch.steps.limit: A batch holds at most {limit} steps
batch.steps.needed: Give at least one step in steps (or stepsFrom) of value
batch.stepsFrom.notJson: The path "{path}" of stepsFrom is not JSON (line {line}, column {column}: {why})
batch.stepsFrom.notSteps: The file of stepsFrom is an array of steps ([{tool, arguments}], at least one)
batch.stepsFrom.tooBig: The path "{path}" of stepsFrom is over the {most} bytes one call may read ({bytes})
batch.tree.gone: This batch's branch no longer exists. Open the batch again with batch
batch.unwritten: Nothing is written. To run it, call batch with target {token} and execute: true (to discard it, give discard: true in value)
batch.unwritten.tried: Nothing is written. The steps were only tried: no batch is open and the tree is not held. To run them, send the same steps again with execute: true. To open a batch and add steps over several calls, give open: true in value
batch.value.branchOnce: branch is named only once, when the batch is opened (this batch writes to {tree})
batch.value.executeOnly: execute: true runs only the steps already staged (give the batch's id as target and no value. To stage steps, leave out execute; to run steps you give right away, leave out target)
batch.value.needsTarget: remove and discard need the batch's id as target
batch.value.oneOnly: Only one of steps, stepsFrom, remove and discard in value can be given at a time
batch.value.openNotExecute: open cannot be combined with execute: true (open starts a batch that holds the tree; execute: true runs). To run an open batch, give its id as target with execute: true
batch.value.otherProject: project differs from this batch's project. A batch works only inside the project it was opened in
